verdict.root_cause: At ~02:26 checkoutservice's outbound CartService/GetCart calls stopped reaching cartservice: the errored client spans are leaves with all duration as self time, no cartservice server span and no Redis child, the signature of a failed dial rather than a slow or erroring cart handler [tr_6a455f48a8d1]. GetCart is the first downstream call in prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart, so every affected PlaceOrder aborts there and the error propagates to frontend, matching frontend's step change at 02:26 and checkoutservice's at 02:26:15 [tr_0ffbbb66e04c][tr_6ca390f6f96d]. I blame cartservice being unreachable. Why it became unreachable is unmeasured: no cartservice metrics, logs, or change history were dispatched, and the change queries covered only frontend and checkoutservice at zero hops [tr_b277d41b4bd4][tr_cb0a259ef1ae].
verdict.reasoning: Only the trace evidence localises the failing hop, and it does so cleanly: errored GetCart client spans with no server-side counterpart mean the request never landed, ruling out cart-internal or Redis slowness [tr_6a455f48a8d1]. Frontend's abrupt change point at 02:26 with partial (~29% peak) errors fits a single dependency failing on cart-touching routes, not a whole-tier outage [tr_0ffbbb66e04c]. checkoutservice is not the originator: it already ran ~21% errors in the baseline, higher than the incident mean, and its logs show routine PlaceOrder entries with 0.1-0.5ms self time [tr_6ca390f6f96d][tr_58d123a13e8f][tr_6a455f48a8d1]. The fault class stays unknown because nothing was measured on cartservice itself to distinguish a crash/OOM loop from a wrong endpoint or lost capacity.
open_questions: No cartservice metrics, logs, pod state, or change history were ever queried - the mechanism behind its unreachability (crashloop, OOM kill, wrong address/port, capacity loss) is entirely unestablished.

The early cluster (~01:58-01:59) failed on ShippingService/GetQuote at the checkoutservice client boundary with a healthy shipping server span; whether that is the same fault, an unrelated pre-existing defect, or a shared network/mesh problem is unresolved.
checkoutservice's ~21% pre-incident error baseline and a traffic gap interval are unexplained and may indicate a longer-running degradation the declared incident window only partly covers.

alternatives.root_cause: A shared network or service-mesh layer began refusing connections from checkoutservice, hitting shipping early and cart late rather than either backend being at fault.
alternatives.why_not: Explains both clusters, but the early shipping traces show a present, non-error shippingservice server span, so those calls did land - unlike the cart calls. The two clusters do not share one signature.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice was killed or throttled after exceeding a memory/CPU limit, so pods stopped accepting connections and checkoutservice's dials failed.
alternatives.why_not: Consistent with the dial-failure signature, but no cartservice resource metric, restart count, or OOM log was ever collected; this is a mechanism hypothesis with zero direct evidence behind it.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is taken, so the observable state should be unchanged: frontend error ratio stays elevated around its post-02:26 level with peaks near 29%, and checkoutservice traces keep showing errored CartService/GetCart leaf spans with no cartservice server span. That continuation is itself the measurement that the diagnosis is still open. The unblocking evidence is narrow and cheap: cartservice container/process state and restart count, cartservice logs across 02:20-02:30, and a change-history query covering cartservice (and the frontend/checkoutservice dependency hops that [tr_b277d41b4bd4] and [tr_cb0a259ef1ae] explicitly never covered). If those show a crashed or crash-looping cartservice process with no recorded change, restart_service on cartservice becomes proposable; if they show a recorded config or image change, revert_config or rollback_image does instead.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if cartservice pod state shows a dead or crash-looping container right now — in that case restart_service was the correct call and the delay cost order throughput. It is also wrong if the failure self-resolves before the follow-up queries land, since then nothing will be left to measure. Conversely, the abstention is vindicated if cartservice is found alive and healthy with its own server spans serving frontend's direct GetCart calls normally, which would place the fault in the checkoutservice→cartservice path (resolution, address, or mesh) where restarting cartservice does nothing observable.
proposal.risk: restart_service on cartservice was considered and rejected on preconditions: the required evidence that the fault is process state rather than a change does not exist — no cartservice metrics, logs, pod state, or change history were ever dispatched. Proposing it anyway carries two specific failure modes. First, the same trace set [tr_6a455f48a8d1] shows the failing hop moved from ShippingService/GetQuote at ~01:59 to CartService/GetCart at ~02:29, both errored at the checkoutservice client boundary with the callee's server span healthy in the shipping case; that pattern is as consistent with a caller-side or network/mesh defect as with cartservice being down, and a cartservice restart would not touch it while creating the false impression the incident was addressed. Second, restart_service is marked irreversible and discards in-process cart state; if cartservice is actually healthy the restart injects a real, avoidable outage into a working service. The cost of this abstention is continued PlaceOrder failures for the minutes it takes to run the missing cartservice queries.
proposal.blast_radius: No service is touched by this proposal. The ongoing, unremediated impact continues to be seen by frontend (whose error ratio stepped at 02:26) and checkoutservice (stepped at 02:26:15), and through frontend by loadgenerator as the traffic source; every PlaceOrder aborts at the first downstream call so currencyservice, productcatalogservice, shippingservice, paymentservice, and emailservice continue to see reduced or absent traffic from checkoutservice rather than errors of their own.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical severity spanning frontend and checkoutservice within thirty seconds, with loadgenerator affected too, describes a real user-facing failure that cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alert pattern alone does not single out a fault class.
